tagline.text: A Ramsar wetland in eastern Mindoro with waterbirds and a hot-spring village

location.label: Location
location.text: Naujan, Victoria, Socorro and Pola, Oriental Mindoro (Barangay Pasi in Socorro is the main land entrance)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: One day or two days and one night

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500~4,000 (day trip from Calapan, including boat and meals)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), then by land and ferry

children.text: Naujan Lake is the fifth-largest freshwater lake in the Philippines, a Ramsar-listed wetland in northeastern Oriental Mindoro. A boat ride on the Butas River, migratory birdwatching and the hot-spring village of Montelago can all be combined on one quiet trip.

Naujan Lake is a large freshwater lake in eastern Mindoro, spread across the four municipalities of Naujan, Victoria, Socorro and Pola in Oriental Mindoro. According to Wikipedia the lake covers about
81km²
(roughly 8,100 ha), making it the fifth largest in the Philippines. It is up to
14km
long and
7km
wide, with a maximum depth reported at about
. Its only outlet is the Butas River, which flows toward the Tablas Strait.

Naujan Lake National Park, which covers the lake and the surrounding forest, was established by Proclamation No. 282 on March 27, 1956, and was listed as a Ramsar wetland on November 12, 1999. It is managed by the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), and tourism activities inside the protected area must be approved by the Protected Area Management Board (PAMB). So think of it not as a resort area packed with amusements, but as a place to slowly take in fishing villages, rice fields and a wetland full of aquatic plants.

The biggest draws here are the birds and the scenery. The western shore is gentle, with wide stretches of shallow water rich in aquatic plants, while the eastern shore is steep and has hot springs. Mount Naujan, an inactive volcano, stands to the northeast of the lake, and geothermal vents have been reported on the eastern slopes. In the protected area you can see waterbirds such as the Philippine duck, the purple swamphen and herons, along with winter migrants, and Mindoro endemics such as the black-hooded coucal are among the area's pride. The surroundings are varied too. According to park information, about

is covered by marsh grass and floating mats of vegetation, and the lake is ringed by forest, grassland, orchards and coconut plantations. Shore residents live by fishing and farming, and the lake is also home to Mindoro's indigenous Mangyan people. In recent years local governments have been developing facilities around the lake to promote tourism, and travel articles have multiplied accordingly. Conditions change quickly here, so check the latest information.

That said, this is not a polished tourist destination. Some facilities are still being prepared, such as the lake-view park and boardwalk in Socorro and the birdwatching tower in Victoria, and some are reportedly not yet fully open. Fees and boat operations change often, so it is safest to ask the national park office first before you go.
From the Butas River dock on the Socorro side, a boat takes you close to waterbirds among the reeds and aquatic plants. The ride to the village of Montelago is described as about
20–30 minutes
. The fare depends on the number of passengers and on negotiation, so confirm it locally.

The lake lies on the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, so many waterbirds visit during the migration season. On the Victoria side there is a birdwatching tower reached by a dirt road through rice fields, and there is also a watch tower near the park office in Pasi, Socorro. Be sure to bring binoculars.

The hot spring in Montelago village on the east side of the lake is very hot thanks to the geothermal zone. Many accounts describe it as a place to enjoy the steam or boil eggs rather than to bathe, so check locally whether soaking is allowed.

blocks.title: Camping and kubo stays in Montelago

children.text: Montelago is described as a quiet, community-run village where you can stay in a tent or a kubo (traditional hut). The sandy lakeshore is enjoyed like a beach, and the mood is peaceful. For bookings, contact the village or the municipal tourism office.
A short walk from the lakeshore on the Pola side leads to Tagbakin Falls, known for its seven tiers. The first tier is said to be about
high. Water volume is greatest just after the rainy season, and you should check the trail condition locally.
In Naujan there is a residents' association that sells crafts made from water lily stems. Lake dishes include tunghod, a native freshwater fish, and ginataang kuhol, snails cooked in coconut milk.

Park information says that the Philippine crocodile and the estuarine crocodile survive in restricted areas, and the lake holds many fish such as mangrove jack, milkfish and tilapia. This is not a place where visitors can see crocodiles, so keep your distance from the water's edge.

items.title: Day itinerary
items.subtitle: From Calapan to Socorro and around the lake

children.text: Set out from central Calapan. Take a modern jeepney bound for Pinamalayan from the Robinsons terminal or the public market and get off in front of the DENR office in Pasi, Socorro.
Stop first at the Naujan Lake National Park office to check which areas are currently open, whether boats are available, and about a guide.
Take a boat from the Butas River dock and go birdwatching around the river and the mouth of the lake. Decide whether to go as far as Montelago after weighing the time and the fare.
Have lunch in Montelago village or in central Socorro. Ask about dishes made with fish from the lake.
Stroll around the lake-view park in Socorro and enjoy the scenery.
Catch a jeepney back to Calapan before dark.

Routes and schedules can change with the time of day, so confirm the last ride back locally in advance. Rather than trying to see the whole lake and every village at once, narrow it down to one boat route and one viewpoint park to keep the day comfortable. Rain affects both boats and walking paths, so keep a backup plan of exploring central Calapan.
Take a boat on the Butas River from Socorro into Montelago.
Look around the area where the hot spring steams, and try boiling eggs where permitted.
Enjoy kayaking or a walk along the lakeshore, then settle into your tent or kubo.
Watch waterbirds on the lake at dawn.
Return by boat to Socorro and head back to Calapan.

Camping and lodging need to be arranged with the village, and how they operate may change. There are no convenience stores by the lake, so bring snacks and drinking water, and be ready for mosquitoes and insects at night. On a clear day you can enjoy the stars and the misty lake at dawn.

Batangas–Calapan ferry times differ by company, so check the latest timetable before departure.
Travel from Puerto Galera by jeepney or bus to the C5 junction (Santa Isabel) in Calapan.
From the C5 junction, take a jeepney or van bound for Pinamalayan and get off in front of DENR in Socorro.
The national road at Pasi, Socorro is the main land entrance to the lake. Stop at the office first for guidance.
Montelago is reached by boat along the Butas River, and boats are arranged locally in the village by negotiation.
There is public transport from Calapan to Naujan town, and one account says tricycles go on to the lake entrance, but fares vary a lot.
The best time for birdwatching is said to be October to March. Some guides note that many migratory birds are seen especially in February and March.
June to November is the rainy season, with higher lake levels and frequent rain. When typhoons pass, boat service may be stopped, so check the weather forecast.

For a day trip, it is comfortable to reach the lake early in the morning, finish the boat ride before noon and rest in central Socorro during the hot midday hours. Birds are most active early in the morning and late in the afternoon, so staying overnight gives you more chances to watch them.

There are almost no large resorts around the lake. In Montelago, staying in a tent or kubo is mentioned, but facilities and prices keep changing, so ask the village or the municipal tourism office in advance. If you want comfort, the realistic choice is to use a hotel or guesthouse in central Calapan as your base and visit as a day trip.

Food centers on simple eateries in the lakeside villages. Locally, the lake's specialties are tunghod, a native freshwater fish, and ginataang kuhol, snails simmered in coconut milk. It is a remote area and there may be no eateries, so bring plenty of water and snacks.

For local food, small eateries in Socorro and Naujan town easily offer grilled dishes and soups. Fish from the lake can be hard to get depending on the season, so ask in advance before ordering. Water lily crafts can be browsed at the residents' association shop in Naujan. Choosing compact souvenirs makes travel easier.
Stop first at the Naujan Lake National Park office in Pasi, Socorro, for guidance. The contact is described as the DENR Socorro office (email naujanlakenp@gmail.com, phone 043-285-7068).
Bringing binoculars and a telephoto lens makes watching the waterbirds far more enjoyable.
Birds are most active early in the morning and around sunset.
Before departing, state the number of people, the time and the route, and agree on a total price for the boat.
Prepare a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen, water and mosquito repellent.
Check the time of the last jeepney back to Calapan in advance.
Places where aquatic plants thrive are habitat for fish and birds, so do not pull up plants from a boat or approach the birds too closely.
If you are introduced to a guide or boat operator through the office, you can avoid unnecessary haggling. Carry cash in small denominations.
The trip to the lake takes a long time, so staying one night in Calapan and starting out in the morning is much more relaxed.
Naujan Lake is a protected area, so do not damage the habitat, and check the latest announcements about entry and boat use.
The hot spring water can be scalding, so do not touch it or get in.
Check that life jackets are worn on boats, and avoid small wooden boats on windy days.
During typhoon season the lake level can rise and roads can be cut off.
There are few official lodgings and restaurants, so carry enough cash and water.
Trails and facilities under development may be closed.
This is the main resort of northern Mindoro, reached via Calapan. Allow at least half a day for the trip.
A place known for diving and beach relaxation.
A large coral reef and diving site in the sea west of Mindoro, reached by boat from the western Mindoro side.
The capital of Oriental Mindoro, with a ferry terminal, lodging and restaurants, makes a good base for a lake trip.
